title: Publish an honest "what Zedu does not do" limits page
description: Buyers find the limits anyway, and every one they discover after signing up costs trust. Publish one page that states plainly what Zedu does not do: the limits on each plan, what it does not replace, and what it does not integrate with yet, each verified against the app rather than guessed. Link it from pricing and the trust page.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Answer "what happens when I reach the limit" for every limit, not only the number
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A table of numbers leaves the reader guessing about the moment the number is reached: does the message send, does the cohort keep working, is anything deleted. Answer that per limit. Work: for each limit the plans publish, write three sentences: what happens at the limit, what happens when someone tries to exceed it, and what the person can do next. Where the answer is not known, test it or mark it as unconfirmed rather than guessing. Deliver the table with a behaviour column for every limit, the tests behind the uncertain ones, and the list of limits where the honest answer is "we do not enforce this yet".

Answering what happens at limits is the most important part of a limits page. Users are not confused by the existence of limits — they are confused by what happens when they hit them. A page that lists limits without explaining the consequence is not actionable.

A number without the behaviour is not a limit a buyer can plan around. Writing what happens at the limit, when someone exceeds it, and what they can do next exposes promises the product does not keep. Marking untested answers as unconfirmed keeps the page honest.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Derive the limits from the code that enforces them, then publish them as one table
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Limits written from memory are the ones that get contradicted by the app in front of a customer. Derive them instead. Work: 1) find every enforcement point: plan gating, seat and cohort caps, upload size, retention of files after a cohort closes, and what an export does and does not include, each with a file reference; 2) separate what is enforced in code from what is only stated in copy, and treat those two lists differently; 3) write the page as one table a buyer can scan, with a plain sentence under it for each limit that needs context; 4) say what Zedu does not replace and does not integrate with yet, checked against the integrations matrix if that exists by then; 5) link it from pricing and the trust page, and give the team a one-line summary of the differences between the table and the current marketing copy. Deliver: the table with evidence per row, the page copy, and the copy-vs-code differences list.
